I am a 53-year-old farmer in the Somali region with no schooling and only a small plot of land. We keep some livestock, so I will spread manure on this maize plot because it costs me nothing, but I cannot afford chemical fertilizer or improved seed from the market. I will sow seeds saved from last season and rely on the rains, as there is no water here for irrigation. My family will do all the work by hand—we cannot pay for hired labor—and I see no need for pesticides on such a small field.
